text:
sara: Heads-up — ran the int6 quant bring-up for zephyrus-emb on staging. Quick summary: overall recall@10 mostly stable, but recall@1 on short (<=6 token) queries dropped ~7 points vs float32. attaching quick plots and examples.

devin: ouch. Is this the short-title cohort we flagged last week? any change in whitening/norming? :thinking:

sara: whitening pipeline unchanged. No PCA. I sliced the paraphrase adversarial set — paraphrase positives are popping out of top1 after quant.

lia: paste a failing example please, helps decide if this is semantic collapse vs rounding noise.

sara: example:
"install node" -> positive: "setup nodejs" -> nearest became: "install python" (unrelated).

ajay: sounds like local neighbor reordering rather than global drift. Could be kernel selection for short seqs in int6 path or KV cache edge-case.

devin: I can repro on local CPU quant runtime. Quick eval snippet I used:

```
# quick recall eval
queries = load_queries('short_queries.json')
emb_q = model.embed(queries, quantize='int6')
emb_db = precomputed_db
sim = topk_cosine(emb_q, emb_db, k=10)
print(recall_at_k(sim, labels, k=1))
```

sara: staging numbers: float32 recall@1 = 0.84, int6 recall@1 = 0.77; int6 recall@10 = 0.92 (float32 0.93).

lia: recall@10 intact suggests jitter in top1 neighbors, not catastrophic manifold shift.

ajay: try UMAP float vs int6 for short queries; check cluster splitting/merging and if paraphrase pairs diverge.

sara: ran UMAP 2d; float clusters dense, int6 shows faint filamentation where paraphrase pairs separate. small shift but enough to flip top1. attaching ascii summary.

devin: hypothesis: quant clipping of vector tails. Experiments: (1) L2-normalize after quant vs before, (2) per-channel scale vs per-tensor scale.

lia: also confirm quant toolchain: onnx int6 or internal packer? per-channel can be unstable for tiny activations.

sara: used internal int6 packer (per-channel symmetric) calibrated on 1k random docs. I'll re-run per-tensor and post-quant L2 norm.

ajay: plan: sara re-run per-tensor + postnorm; devin repros CPU with both packer variants; lia generates UMAP diffs and a pivot table of recall@1 by query-length bins. We'll run a focused paraphrase adversarial set of 200 pairs for a hard check.

sara: starting re-runs now, ETA ~2 hours.

eval-bot: automation: started job zephyrus-int6-rt1 with tags [per-tensor,postnorm]. job_id=98312

sara: quick results (smoke): per-tensor int6 + post-L2 -> recall@1 = 0.82 (up from 0.77), recall@10 = 0.915, nearest-swap rate down ~40% vs per-channel.

devin: nice. points to per-channel calibration instability on short activations. can you measure throughput/latency impact of per-tensor vs per-channel?

lia: I'll produce pivot table: recall@1 by length bins (<=6, 7-16, 17+), and UMAP float vs int6 overlays for the paraphrase set. If per-tensor+postnorm scales to larger evals, add a policy: for short-query-heavy workloads prefer per-tensor quant + postnorm.

ajay: add onboarding checklist item: "paraphrase adversarial recall@1 by length bins" to catch regressions like this.

sara: will update zephyrus onboarding PR with failing examples, plots, and mitigation notes.

devin: ping me when PR is ready; I'll sanity-check throughput impact.

sara: thanks all :thumbsup:
